title: Random user ID generator
description:
Write a function which generates a six digit/character random_user_id.

```py
  print(random_user_id())
  '1ee33d'
```

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as random_user_id(seed=None). When seed is provided, seed the random module with it first (for deterministic testing) before generating the id; return the 6-character id as a string built from lowercase letters and digits.
starter_code:
import random
import string

def random_user_id(seed=None):
    # your code here
    pass
hints: Import both the random and string modules - string gives you ready-made character pools like string.ascii_lowercase and string.digits.
If seed is not None, call random.seed(seed) before doing any random generation so the output becomes reproducible.
Build a pool of allowed characters, then use a loop or a generator expression with random.choice() to pick 6 characters and join them into one string.
expected_behavior: Returns a 6-character string made of lowercase letters and digits. When called with the same seed, always returns the exact same id.

hidden_tests.label: seed 0 produces the expected deterministic id
seed 42 produces the expected deterministic id
generated id is always 6 characters long

explanation: random.seed(seed) puts the pseudo-random generator into a known, reproducible state, so random.choice() then returns the same sequence of characters every time for that seed. string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits gives the pool of allowed characters, and joining 6 random picks from it produces the id.
